status: Research candidate pool; no released learning path or verified song arrangements
selection: 50 public electric-rock titles + 49 public three-chord titles + Wonderwall from the strumming collection

sources.title: First 50 Rock Songs You Should Play on Electric Guitar
sources.selection_basis: Published guitar repertoire list; not a popularity ranking or graded course

sources.title: The Guitar Three-Chord Songbook
sources.selection_basis: Publisher describes simplified G/C/D arrangements; that does not establish chords/key for an original recording
sources.public_list_note: 49 distinct titles displayed on the inspected page despite a 50-song description; no missing entry invented

sources.title: First 50 Songs You Should Strum on Guitar
sources.selection_basis: Wonderwall retained from founder feedback and present in the published strumming collection

first_review_batch.status: Proposed research priority, not verified easiest-to-hardest order
first_review_batch.scope: Reuse the three existing examples, then inspect seven candidate recordings/teaching variants before acquisition or learner publication

proposed_practice_tracks.goal: Consistent downstrokes, then easier changes among a few playable open shapes
Start with a short single-note pattern, then add movable power shapes and muting

curation_policy.title_identity: Resolve artist, exact version, tuning and capo before creating a recording-specific chart; titles such as Jailbreak or Gloria are ambiguous
curation_policy.difficulty: Grade actual fingerings/transitions/tempo/rhythm; number of chord names alone is insufficient
curation_policy.chart_inputs: Public song membership supplies no recording-specific chord/key/time reference; source transpositions are hypotheses
curation_policy.reference_evaluation: Use annotated or independently checked version-matched material; proposed catalogue is not an accuracy benchmark
curation_policy.founder_workflow: Prepare drafts automatically; optional issue tap, with no required transcription
